assertion.statement: For each good place of the actual A/K above p outside T and every coefficient prime ell different from p, inertia acts trivially on V_ell(A).
assertion.objects: The original abelian surface A/K and its actual ell-adic Tate module at a good place above p.
assertion.hypotheses: A has the established good abelian model at that place and ell differs from p. The local field has its usual strict henselization.
assertion.quantifiers: Every such place and each coefficient prime ell different from p.
assertion.parameter_range: Good finite places of the actual number field K; no claim at ell=p.
assertion.uniformity: No additional exceptional primes or field replacement.
assertion.normalizations: Actual torsion of A with multiplication transition maps.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Bad reduction and residue-characteristic torsion are excluded.
assertion.limit_order: Finite-etale torsion splits over the strict henselization at every level, then pass to the inverse limit. The separate induced representation argument follows.

use.reason: Apply the existing prime-to-residue-characteristic finite-etale specialization argument to this actual good A/K. Torsion over the strict henselization is unramified at every ell-power level, hence inertia fixes its Tate module. This is the good-reduction implication cited in the manuscript; no assertion about the induced representation or endomorphism lattice follows without the separate arguments.

supplier.statement: Prime-to-residue-characteristic torsion of a good abelian scheme specializes bijectively over the strict henselian base, compatibly with transition maps and homomorphisms.
